provenance.method: GPT-6 Pro selected in Chrome; completed Deep Research report and DOM table extraction
provenance.researchBackendModel: not exposed by the Deep Research UI
provenance.status: review questions and proposed thresholds; not measured results or authoritative oracle

questions.question: Does v0.4.0 improve fixed-model DeepSWE outcomes at all?
questions.hypothesis: Current plugin has positive paired effect over no-plugin Codex.
questions.metric: Per-task verifier binary reward and pass fractions; paired treatment-control delta.
questions.experiment: Frozen 20 tasks, one attempt/arm, exact current plugin.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: No positive quality signal while median time ratio >1.10.
questions.confounds: Model stochasticity; task heterogeneity; order/cache effects.

questions.question: Is semantic advice better than identical integration overhead?
questions.hypothesis: Real advice beats a neutral-message placebo.
questions.metric: Paired verifier reward, harmful-advice task rate, recovery, action counts.
questions.experiment: Keep hooks/provider calls; replace model-visible result with fixed neutral content.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: Real ≤ placebo on quality with equal or worse cost.
questions.confounds: Perfect latency/token matching is hard.

questions.question: Is task-matched advice better than plausible wrong advice?
questions.hypothesis: Correctly matched advice beats precommitted shuffled advice.
questions.metric: Same task-level outcomes plus uptake/harm.
questions.experiment: Supply same-format advice sampled from a precommitted event-type-matched pool unrelated to current task.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: Matched ≤ shuffled.
questions.confounds: Advice distributions may differ unless carefully matched.

questions.question: How often do automatic hooks lack real candidate catalogs?
questions.hypothesis: Most useful events have real, event-relevant candidate sets.
questions.metric: candidateCatalog.provided/source/count by event; task-level percentage with fallback.
questions.experiment: Log the existing invocation field on dev suite and primary run.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: >50% of decision-bearing calls use fallback; >80% is severe.
questions.confounds: Some generic gates may still be useful.

questions.question: Does a real candidate catalog improve decisions?
questions.hypothesis: Replacing generic meta-actions with actual viable actions raises oracle accuracy and task utility.
questions.metric: Labeled dev decisions; task reward when promoted.
questions.experiment: Candidate-rich vs current payload, same event/timing.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: No reduction in decision error or no downstream benefit.
questions.confounds: Quality of candidate generator itself.

questions.question: Does the current renderer throw away custom choices?
questions.hypothesis: Arbitrary selected candidates are visible and actionable to Codex.
questions.metric: Compare provider choice to exact model-visible message and next action.
questions.experiment: Dev fixture with candidate IDs outside fixed generic actions.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: Any assessed custom choice that cannot be recovered from the message.
questions.confounds: None if fixture is deterministic.

questions.question: Does an actionable renderer help independently of payload quality?
questions.hypothesis: Concrete deterministic advice beats current status/decision/confidence rendering using the same Jev result.
questions.metric: Recovery rate, harmful advice, unnecessary actions, task reward.
questions.experiment: Current payload/Jev answer; alternate renderer only.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: No improvement, or more harm.
questions.confounds: Renderer itself can contain useful heuristics unrelated to Jev.

questions.question: Are lifecycle checkpoints placed where advice can still change behavior?
questions.hypothesis: A high fraction of assessed advice has a real downstream decision opportunity.
questions.metric: Same-event lineage: advisory → next model/tool action; “action opportunity” rate.
questions.experiment: Instrument all current event types.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: <50% of assessed calls have a plausible subsequent decision before task end; stop-time >90% no-next-action is strong failure.
questions.confounds: A message can affect final text without another tool.

questions.question: Do selective checkpoints dominate blanket lifecycle advice?
questions.hypothesis: Calling Jev only at uncertainty/failure/completion-risk points preserves or improves quality with materially less overhead.
questions.metric: Task reward, calls/task, wall time, token deltas, harmful advice.
questions.experiment: Current all-events vs fixed local trigger policy.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: Selective gives same/better quality and ≥25% fewer provider calls: blanket policy fails value test.
questions.confounds: Trigger policy may itself encode useful logic.

questions.question: Does batched atomic questioning outperform one broad meta-choice?
questions.hypothesis: Choice/Noul/Score fan-out gives lower labeled error and equal/lower latency than separate/general decisions.
questions.metric: Dev Brier/selective error, task recovery, provider calls and latency.
questions.experiment: Same event/state; current classifier vs one batch of atomic questions.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: Current classifier has materially higher labeled error or equivalent quality at higher cost.
questions.confounds: Question wording; deterministic combination rule.

questions.question: Can stale root objectives change advice after a task switch?
questions.hypothesis: Starting a new task in one session cannot make old task state alter the new recommendation.
questions.metric: Payload root/latest fields; recommendation under clean vs reused scope.
questions.experiment: Two unrelated deterministic dev tasks back-to-back, with/without reset.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: Any reproducible recommendation change attributable to old goal; >5% across switch fixtures fails.
questions.confounds: Genuine cross-task continuity can sometimes be intended.

questions.question: Do persisted candidate catalogs go stale?
questions.hypothesis: A catalog never crosses into a new incompatible objective.
questions.metric: Candidate IDs valid for current task; stale-catalog rate.
questions.experiment: Same task-switch suite, seed a catalog in first task.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: Any stale candidate selected; >1% stale exposure is unacceptable.
questions.confounds: Scope semantics.

questions.question: Does automatic PostToolUse see enough failure state?
questions.hypothesis: Known command failures are represented as failures rather than innocuous output.
questions.metric: Deterministic failing commands with varied stdout/stderr; false-proceed rate.
questions.experiment: Dev fixtures: nonzero exit, empty stdout, misleading success text, partial error.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: >5% assessed proceed on clearly failed fixture.
questions.confounds: Host's exact tool-result schema.

questions.question: Does bounded context remove decisive evidence?
questions.hypothesis: Advice is invariant when nonessential state forces compaction.
questions.metric: Presence of tagged decisive field; choice/probability changes under harmless padding.
questions.experiment: Insert long irrelevant logs before/after a known decisive constraint.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: >5% semantic flip or any systematic loss of a required constraint.
questions.confounds: Jev itself can react to distractors even if field survives.

questions.question: Is the 0.6 confidence/probability gate safe for this use case?
questions.hypothesis: At default thresholds, assessed advice has acceptably low labeled error.
questions.metric: Coverage vs error curve; selected probability and confidence analyzed separately.
questions.experiment: Labeled disjoint dev event set.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: >5% high-confidence harmful assessments, or another threshold strictly dominates risk/coverage.
questions.confounds: Dev labels may not represent DeepSWE.

questions.question: Does the plugin's overhead buy any quality?
questions.hypothesis: Any material time/token cost accompanies a material outcome or recovery gain.
questions.metric: Paired turn/wall ratios and task outcomes.
questions.experiment: Primary 20 pairs.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: Median turn ratio >1.10 and no quality/recovery signal.
questions.confounds: Provider load; pair order.

questions.question: Does plugin installation increase Codex context size?
questions.hypothesis: Added context is small enough not to change model behavior through token load alone.
questions.metric: Input, cached input, uncached input, output and peak context per task.
questions.experiment: Current primary pair.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: >10% input increase without quality value.
questions.confounds: Task trajectories naturally change token use.

questions.question: Is prompt-cache churn actually occurring?
questions.hypothesis: Treatment reduces cache effectiveness after controlling task/order.
questions.metric: Uncached-input ratio, cached-input share, order interaction.
questions.experiment: Counterbalanced pairs; log cache tokens each model call if available.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: Treatment uncached input >10% above baseline consistently.
questions.confounds: Provider cache opaque; second arm may inherit warm prefixes.

questions.question: Are most Jev calls redundant confirmations?
questions.hypothesis: Consecutive assessed calls often change or refine the workflow rather than echoing proceed.
questions.metric: Per-task decision sequence; fraction of calls followed by no detectable behavior change.
questions.experiment: Existing instrumentation plus next-action lineage.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: >70% assessed calls are same generic choice with no observable action effect.
questions.confounds: Correct confirmation can still prevent rare errors.

questions.question: Are abstentions targeted at genuinely ambiguous states?
questions.hypothesis: Ambiguous cases abstain more often than clear cases while clear correct cases retain coverage.
questions.metric: Selective risk/coverage on labeled dev events.
questions.experiment: Construct clear and ambiguous pairs.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: Clear-case abstention >20% or ambiguous high-confidence error >5%.
questions.confounds: Ambiguity labels.

questions.question: What caused the four nonvalidated/unavailable pilot receipts?
questions.hypothesis: Failure rate is low, understood and non-correlated with difficult events.
questions.metric: Reason code/schema/transport class per failed receipt.
questions.experiment: Make reason attribution mandatory in next run.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: >1% unexplained provider-result failures, or concentration at critical checkpoints.
questions.confounds: Rare network/provider incidents.

questions.question: Can every explicit MCP call be tied to its provider result?
questions.hypothesis: All treatment decisions have complete call→receipt lineage.
questions.metric: MCP request ID → receipt ID join success.
questions.experiment: Add correlation ID before the DeepSWE run.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: Anything below 100% for study records.
questions.confounds: Cached/local-only MCP operations need explicit status.

questions.question: Can each model-visible advisory be tied to the next action?
questions.hypothesis: Every assessed message has a unique same-task lineage into subsequent observable behavior.
questions.metric: event_id → receipt_id → message_hash → next_action_id.
questions.experiment: Telemetry only; no prompt changes.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: <95% linkability.
questions.confounds: Parallel/subagent actions require explicit scope IDs.

questions.question: Does reconsider prevent good actions?
questions.hypothesis: High-confidence negative advice rarely causes an unnecessary detour from an action that would have succeeded.
questions.metric: Proposed action, advice, changed action, eventual verifier evidence.
questions.experiment: Dev cases with known-good proposed action plus DeepSWE descriptive analysis.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: Harm on >5% of labeled good-action events.
questions.confounds: Counterfactual success often unknowable on natural tasks.

questions.question: Does the plugin improve recovery after genuine failures?
questions.hypothesis: Treatment more often and more quickly reaches a correct state after a real tool/test failure.
questions.metric: Task-level recovery yes/no; actions/time from first failure to successful check/final pass.
questions.experiment: Deterministic injected failures on dev suite; observational DeepSWE secondary metric.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: No improvement or longer recovery.
questions.confounds: Natural failures are endogenous to prior model behavior.

questions.question: Does the plugin reduce false completion?
questions.hypothesis: Jev-treated runs less often stop while the independent verifier later fails.
questions.metric: agent_finished ∧ verifier_fail, stratified by last Jev completion/stop signal.
questions.experiment: Primary DeepSWE plus deterministic incomplete dev tasks.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: Any systematic proceed/supported signal before verifier failure; no reduction vs baseline.
questions.confounds: Hidden tests are intentionally unavailable to agent.

questions.question: Does the plugin reduce missed explicit constraints?
questions.hypothesis: Treatment violates fewer prompt-stated constraints.
questions.metric: Blind checklist derived solely from public task instruction, not reference solution; verifier result.
questions.experiment: Human/deterministic post-hoc audit blinded to arm.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: No reduction or new constraint violations.
questions.confounds: Checklist subjectivity; verifier may already cover constraint.

questions.question: Does the Interrupt domain mismatch matter?
questions.hypothesis: Strategy catalogs work during Interrupt despite current domain mapping.
questions.metric: Which domain/catalog reaches request and selected choice.
questions.experiment: Deterministic interrupt fixture with distinct strategy and result catalogs.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: Strategy catalog not used when required.
questions.confounds: Host may rarely expose Interrupt in target workflow.

questions.question: Does catalog-source telemetry tell us where candidates came from?
questions.hypothesis: We can distinguish persisted task catalog, raw host catalog and fallback.
questions.metric: Provenance label vs injected source in fixtures.
questions.experiment: Feed each source path separately.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: Any source ambiguity that prevents diagnosis.
questions.confounds: Does not affect task behavior itself.

questions.question: Do hosted/special tool paths bypass automation often enough to matter?
questions.hypothesis: Current hooks cover most decision-bearing tool activity in target Codex runs.
questions.metric: Hookable tool actions / all observable tool actions per task.
questions.experiment: Coverage audit on DeepSWE trajectories.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: <95% of target decision-bearing actions observable to integration.
questions.confounds: Some bypassed actions need no Jev advice.

questions.question: Is advice stable to irrelevant-state perturbation?
questions.hypothesis: Adding semantically irrelevant state does not flip a high-confidence decision.
questions.metric: Choice flip rate, probability drift.
questions.experiment: Dev metamorphic tests with duplicated logs, irrelevant filenames and reordered harmless fields.
questions.proposedFailureThreshold: >5% high-confidence flips.
questions.confounds: Some “irrelevant” fields may accidentally add meaning.
